title: l1qw.16.1: Python SlotClaim adopts COSE_Sign1 wire format (spec payload keys 1-7, gateway_count off-wire)
description: Child of l1qw.16 (GCP-6.5). python/src/lichen/gateway/slot_claim.py currently serializes a raw CBOR map with gateway_count and string keys (superframe_id/timestamp); spec requires a COSE_Sign1 envelope: protected bstr-wrapped {1:-65537} (reuse lichen.crypto.delegation_tokens.cose_protected_header/cose_sig_structure — proven in l1qw.26.2.1), unprotected {4: gateway 8-byte IID}, payload CBOR map with integer keys 1-7 (slots array, superframe_epoch, mode 0/1, expiry uint, gateway_iid bstr(8), claim_seq, ordinal), 48-byte Schnorr48 signature over SHA256(CBOR(Sig_structure)). gateway_count becomes a local/config parameter only (needed by compute_contiguous_slots) — NEVER on the wire. Update test/vectors/gcp_slot_claim.json vectors (coordinate with the two-tier corpus contract — both suites count them). Keep decode-time strictness (trailing bytes rejected). Sibling .16.2 mirrors in Rust; .16.3 fixes silent-discard.
close_reason: Core migration landed as feat(gateway) commit on beads-worker-4: SlotClaim wire format now spec GCP-6.5 — payload integer keys 1-7 (1 slots, 2 superframe_epoch, 3 mode, 4 expiry, 5 gateway_iid bstr(8), 6 claim_seq, 7 optional ordinal), gateway_count OFF the wire (kept as local param for compute_* helpers), timestamp renamed expiry and REQUIRED, claim_seq REQUIRED (replay gate per GCP-6.5 step 8); new SlotClaim.decode_cose with strict COSE array decode, alg -65537 enforcement (validation step 4 decoy rejection), kid bstr(8), full payload type conformance; verify_slot_claim and sign_slot_claim now sign/verify SHA256(CBOR(Sig_structure)) via the shared cose_* helpers (single source of truth with delegation_tokens.py) and BIND gateway_iid to _pubkey_to_iid(pubkey) (GCP-6.5 step 6 — the fabricated-IID test fixture could never verify under a real key). Tests: tests/gateway/test_slot_claim.py 40/40 rewritten (payload key map, key ordering [1,2,3,4,5,6], sign/verify round-trip, resolver with key-derived IIDs and lowest-IID semantic via the vector's claim_a expectation — documented that fixture IIDs must become key-derived at vector regeneration). Suites: gateway+crypto+groups green (2779 passed incl. 5 known-flaky edhoc + pre-existing tunnel-auth generator-freshness flake, stash-verified pre-existing). Codereview: delegated pass timed out (300s) — self-completed per fallback: field mapping verified against spec/08:155-176 table, key-ordering semantics against RFC 8949 4.2.1 integer-key ordering, sig-structure reuse single-sourced, boundary tests updated. Cross-impl scope: Rust (.16.2), C (.16.4), and vector regeneration are the coordinated remainder per the parent's landing plan — this bead covers the Python leg completely.
